title: Envelope encryption
description: Data is encrypted with a unique data key; the data key is then encrypted with a master key and stored alongside the ciphertext. Decryption unwraps the data key first, then the data. Envelope encryption limits master-key use and makes per-record keys practical. (Demos illustrate the key hierarchy with a teaching cipher; production uses AES-GCM via a vetted library.) At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers per-record data keys wrapped by a master key.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: b"hi", 2: b"hello world", 3: b"archive record 12345"}
import os, hashlib, hmac
# teaching illustration of envelope structure (NOT production crypto)
master = os.urandom(16)
data_key = os.urandom(16)
def wrap(k, m): return bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(k, hashlib.sha256(m).digest()[:16]))
def enc(pt, k): return bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(pt, hashlib.sha256(k).digest() * 4))[:len(pt)]
ct = enc(CFG[LEVEL], data_key)
wrapped = wrap(data_key, master)
dk2 = wrap(wrapped, master)  # unwrap
pt2 = enc(ct, dk2)
print("roundtrip ok:", pt2 == CFG[LEVEL], "| wrapped key len:", len(wrapped))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Key rotation
description: Keys are replaced on a schedule or on suspicion of compromise. During rotation both old and new keys can decrypt (dual-read) while new data uses only the new key; afterwards data is re-encrypted or the old key is retired. Rotation bounds the damage of any single key exposure. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers scheduled and emergency rotation.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Key hierarchy
description: Keys are organized in a hierarchy: a master key protects key-encrypting keys, which protect data keys. Compromise of a data key exposes one record; compromise higher up is contained by separation of duties and hardware protection. The hierarchy mirrors the blast radius it contains. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers master, key-encrypting, and data key tiers.

title: Authorized crypto operations
description: Every encrypt, decrypt, wrap, and unwrap call is authorized against the caller's identity and logged with the key id and purpose. Unauthorized calls are denied before touching key material. The operation log is the audit trail for all cryptographic activity. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers authorizing each operation by identity.

title: Key destruction ceremony
description: Key destruction is a witnessed procedure: all copies are overwritten, hardware slots are zeroized, and witnesses attest the destruction in a signed record. Cryptographic erasure (destroying the key) renders ciphertext unrecoverable even where copies of the ciphertext remain. The ceremony record is archived permanently. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers overwriting all key copies.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 3}
copies = ["copy-%d" % i for i in range(CFG[LEVEL])]
witnesses = ["w1", "w2"]
destroyed = ["\x00" * 8 for _ in copies]  # overwrite
attested = all(c == "\x00" * 8 for c in destroyed) and len(witnesses) >= 2
print("copies destroyed:", len(destroyed), "| witnesses:", witnesses, "| ceremony complete:", attested)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
